look_here_first: Inspect the resinous head, stem surface, and mature cypsela: yellow rays around a disk, serrate leaves clasping the stem, glabrous-to-nearly-glabrous gland-dotted stems, and a pappus with numerous bristles. Do not identify from yellow color alone.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved source pool / Master Plant Pool
project_inclusion.range_basis: B062 deep review verifies Hays County under the current accepted concept; fewer than three exact target-zone native counties confirmed. Historical Grindelia papposa maps as a synonym; do not count unreconciled old concepts as independent county evidence.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Not counted as a confirmed target-zone native unless a separate three-county PASS review is completed.

best_field_traits: Annual herb with branching flowering stems; inspect base and mature shoots.
Alternate, toothed, sessile-to-clasping leaves; resin dots often visible.
Radiate yellow heads with sticky involucral phyllaries.
Stems largely glabrous apart from resin glands; compare hairiness directly.
Mature fruit with multiple pappus bristles; magnification useful.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus G. adenodonta, examine stem hairs (adenodonta noticeably hairy/glandular-hairy; ciliata generally glabrous and gland-dotted) and mature pappus. G. nuda is typically rayless, so check head for rays. G. lanceolata has narrower leaves and perennial habit; use stem and head together. G. squarrosa often has strongly reflexed squarrose phyllaries; its historical var. nuda belongs to G. nuda, not this card.
